description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of three prompting strategies—“Basic prompt” (dark blue), “Structured prompt + oracle” (orange), and “Structured prompt + predicted” (dark green)—across two large language models, GPT-4o and Sonnet, with an unlabeled baseline group on the far left. The vertical axis represents a performance metric ranging from 0 to 0.7 in increments of 0.1, though no unit or specific metric (e.g., F1-score, accuracy) is labeled. For GPT-4o, the “Structured prompt + oracle” achieves the highest score at approximately 0.58, followed by “Structured prompt + predicted” at ~0.47, and “Basic prompt” at ~0.26. For Sonnet, “Structured prompt + oracle” again performs best at ~0.52, followed by “Structured prompt + predicted” at ~0.42, and “Basic prompt” at ~0.34. The unlabeled group on the left shows “Basic prompt” at ~0.32, “Structured prompt + oracle” at ~0.60, and “Structured prompt + predicted” at ~0.35. The chart suggests that structured prompting with oracle input consistently outperforms other methods across models, while the predicted variant shows moderate gains over basic prompting. The bars are grouped by model (or condition) along the horizontal axis, with color-coded legends clearly indicating each strategy. No error bars or statistical significance markers are present.
